name: CO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Kiros's large fundraising advantage over Peterson
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 97%
Open seat after DeGette lost renomination
model.rationale: CO-01's D+29 lean makes a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely, and Melat Kiros has raised over $1 million with heavy outside spending while Republican Christy Peterson has raised about $2,000. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays at Safe D.
model.watch: A surprise collapse in Democratic turnout or a major scandal involving Kiros would be the main route to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Diana DeGette (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Denver-based CO-01 is one of the most Democratic districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+29. Longtime incumbent Diana DeGette is not on the ballot after losing renomination, but the seat remains firmly in Democratic hands on paper. Democrat Melat Kiros has raised over $1.1 million and benefits from substantial outside spending on both sides, while Republican Christy Peterson has raised only about $2,000. Minor-party and independent candidates are on the ballot but lack the resources to matter.

Prediction markets give the Democratic candidate roughly a 97% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals. With no public polling and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on the district's lean and the lopsided money race, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
